messages.text: I’m using the `create-javafx-app` skill to scaffold Gymmie with Gradle, JavaFX, Checkstyle, JaCoCo, tests, Shadow JAR packaging, CI, and the requested starter files. I’ll first inspect the repository, then create and verify the project in place.

The repository is essentially empty and has the required JDK 25. The system Gradle executable is present but cannot load its macOS ARM native library, so I’m checking the installed Gradle setup before scaffolding to ensure the generated wrapper can still be used reliably.

The wrapper task needs a minimal Gradle build to exist first, so I’m adding the project definition and source layout now; then I’ll regenerate the wrapper at 9.7.1 and run the full verification tasks through `./gradlew`. I’ll keep the package name `com.gymmie` and the UI intentionally minimal as requested.

The project files and Gradle 9.7.1 wrapper have been generated successfully. The first wrapper invocation exposed the same sandbox restriction on the default `~/.gradle` cache, so I’m using a repository-local Gradle cache for verification; this keeps the wrapper reproducible without relying on inaccessible global state.

The first validation run found two concrete issues: one 102-character source line, and Gradle 9.7.1 requires an explicit JUnit Platform launcher on the test runtime classpath. I’m correcting both, then I’ll rerun `check` and build the Shadow JAR.

`./gradlew check` and `./gradlew shadowJar` now pass. I’m doing the final runtime smoke test and checking that every requested file and artifact is present; the runtime task is expected to stay open while the JavaFX window is running.

The runtime task reached the JavaFX application, but this sandbox has no usable display surface, so JavaFX’s renderer reported an environment-level screen error and I stopped the still-running process. The compile, resource loading, tests, Checkstyle, and Shadow packaging all pass; I’m now doing artifact/file checks and cleaning the local verification cache from the project’s untracked files.

Created the Gymmie JavaFX app with:

- Gradle 9.7.1 wrapper
- JavaFX starter UI displaying “Gymmie”
- Checkstyle, JaCoCo, JUnit 5, and Shadow JAR
- GitHub Actions workflow
- README, AGENTS.md, and `.gitignore`

Validation passed:

- `./gradlew check`
- `./gradlew shadowJar`
- Fat JAR: [Gymmie-1.0.0.jar](/Users/shawnnygoh/github-repos/CS3227-2610-MP2/build/libs/Gymmie-1.0.0.jar)

The runtime smoke test reached the JavaFX app, but this environment has no display surface for rendering the window.

---
name: create-javafx-app
description: Scaffold a new JavaFX desktop app with a small, consistent project structure.
---

## When to use this

Use when you need to set up a new JavaFX desktop app.

## What to build

Create a JavaFX project and add a starter scene as an entry point. Keep it minimal.

## Prerequisites

- JDK 25
- Gradle 9.7.1
- A GitHub repository already initialized

## Steps

1. Scaffold the JavaFX app with Gradle by running `gradle :wrapper --gradle-version 9.7.1` and apply the necessary plugins (e.g. OpenJFX JavaFX Plugin 0.1.0, Gradle Shadow 9.6.1).

2. Add style checks following the se-education.org Java coding standard.

3. Add Jacoco for measuring code coverage.

4. Add Shadow Gradle and verify that `./gradlew shadowJar` produces a runnable fat jar.

5. Add JUnit 5 and write one trivial test.

6. Create App.java, Launcher.java, MainController.java and MainWindow.fxml which contains a minimal UI with a title label that displays the app's name. Style the UI with CSS.

7. Add a GitHub Actions workflow that checks out the repo, sets up the JDK and runs `./gradlew check`.

8. Add AGENTS.md which includes the tech stack, build commands (`./gradlew run`, `./gradlew check`, `./gradlew shadowJar`), code style convention, and git convention.

9. Add a minimal README.md which includes the project name, a one-line description, and how to build and run the app.

10. Add a .gitignore which excludes any `build/`, `.gradle/` or IDE folders.

## Project structure after setup

- src/
    - main/java/<package>/
        - App.java
        - MainController.java
        - Launcher.java (entry)
    - main/resources/<package>/
        - view/
            - MainWindow.fxml (root UI)
        - css/
            - <package>.css
    - test/java/<package>/
        - TrivialTest.java
- gradle/
    - wrapper/
        - gradle-wrapper.jar
        - gradle-wrapper.properties
- config/
    - checkstyle/
        - checkstyle.xml
        - suppressions.xml
- build.gradle
- settings.gradle
- gradlew.bat
- gradlew
- README.md
- AGENTS.md
- .gitignore
- .github/workflows/gradle.yml

## Definition of done

- `./gradlew run` launches the application window without errors
- `./gradlew check` passes (Checkstyle and tests both pass)
- `./gradlew shadowJar` produces a runnable fat jar in `build/libs/`
- All files mentioned in the project structure above exist
